recipes.name: Jennie's Heavenly Slow Cooker Chicken
ingredients_raw: 1 (10.75 ounce) can condensed golden mushroom soup
1 (8 ounce) container chive and onion cream cheese
1 (.7 ounce) package dry Italian-style salad dressing mix

steps.text: Melt butter in a saucepan over medium heat; stir in mushroom soup, cream cheese, wine, and salad dressing mix until hot, smooth, and combined.
Place chicken breasts in the bottom of a slow cooker; pour cream cheese sauce over top. Cover slow cooker. Cook on Low until chicken is tender, about 4 hours.

raw_recipe.headline: Jennie's Heavenly Slow Cooker Chicken
raw_recipe.description: Jennie's heavenly slow-cooker chicken recipe gently cooks chicken breasts in a cream cheese, mushroom soup, Italian dressing mix, and white wine sauce.

video.description: Watch how to make this heavenly chicken dish. The chicken breasts are cooked in a creamy mushroom and cheese sauce until perfectly tender. And because the cooking takes place in a slow cooker, you know it's going to be perfectly tender and still juicy. Serve over rice, pasta, or potatoes.

review.reviewBody: I make this ALL the time. Its the best slow cooker recipe ever! The only thing I change is I use chicken broth instead of white wine, and I use regular cream of mushroom soup- it has a better flavor than the golden mushroom soup. I always serve over angel hair pasta with a nice crusty bread to soak up the fabulous sauce. This is one of my all time favorite recipes!! I cook on high for 3-4 hours, OR on low for 6-8 hours.

great but easier version is: pan fry sliced onion & mushrooms in butter, then add chicken sprinkled with a lot of italian spices & fresh ground pepper, brown both sides. Add 2 cans regular mushroom soup, the chive & onion cream cheese (if you have only regular cream cheese use that) a few TB sour cream, heat through, add wine but it's better with about 1/3 cup sherry. Serve with cut-up fresh chives& parsley. Great with mashed potatoes or served on heated pastry shells.We like a lot of sauce, so you can play around by adding or deleting. Only takes about 20 min from start to finish and it's unbelievably great.

Oh Jennie, this was wonderful and SO easy! I doubled the recipe because we like to have enough for lunch the next day. I only used one package of Italian dressing, and it was perfect. If I had used two, I'm sure it would still have been delightful. I did saute one finely chopped onion and 6 cloves of garlic in the butter. Then added Chardonnay and let that simmer for about 10 minutes before adding the soup and cream cheese. I only had one can of Golden Mushroom so I had to use a can of Cream of Chicken (all I had left) as well. Cut my chicken breasts into large chunks (I butcher my breasts to begin with getting all that gross cartilage stuff out). Then I seasoned them directly with a quarter of that Italian seasoning packet as well as some garlic powder and oregano. The rest of that packet went into the soup mixture. I didn't have enough cream cheese to double the amount along with the rest of my ingredients, so right before it was done, I shredded some fresh parmegano-reggiano into it to try to mimic having the full amount of cream cheese. Also, I steamed some fresh broccoli and threw that in about 10 minutes before serving. And lastly, I added four Calabrian peppers (packed in oil) to the mixture with the broccoli to render a little flavorful heat. Served over fettucine. I licked my plate. Thanks so much Jennie - this is a winner!

My husband and I loved this recipe. I did adapt it somewhat. I used regular cream cheese and freeze dried chives. I added 1/4 cup diced onions to the butter and sautéed them before adding the rest. I also added a small can of sliced mushrooms. The chicken was cubed because my husband prefers it. I forgot this was a crock pot recipe so at 4 PM my go to was the instant pot. I sautéed the chicken in the pot before adding the sauce and pressure cooked it for 15 minutes. Delicious over white rice.

Loved it! Husband said, "Perfect winter comfort food." Googled "substitute for dry Italian-style salad dressing mix" and used 1/2 t Frontier all purpose seasoning and salt, and 1/4 oregano, garlic powder, and black pepper. I used Pacific Foods cream of chicken soup. I used chicken tenders and it took about 4 hours on Low. Added 30 grams of grated Parmesan cheese at the very end.

This is a fantastic dish, my whole family loves it. First time only change was to substitute chicken broth for the wine. Second time I made it I put the crock pot on high and added the butter, italian dressing mix, cream cheese, soup, and broth and let it melt, stirred it to blend, then added the chicken. Saved me washing another pan :). We like it over rice or noodles.

This is so easy and it turned out great. I’m recently widowed and looking for easy comfort food recipes. This fit the bill. I used the spicy version of the Italian dressing dry mix and it was fine. Did this in my Ninja Foodi Deluxe using the slow cooker setting on low for 4 hours. Chicken breasts were perfect. I did check with a thermometer to make sure they were at 165 degrees. Enjoy! I’ll make it again!

I used the recipe but doubled it because we chose to make portobello mushroom ravioli to go with the chicken rather than rice and it was a good decision with this phenominal sauce. What we changed in the recipe were substitutions. I didn't have enough of the cream cheese so I added 8 oz of sour cream and it turned out wonderful. Depending on how thick your chicken breasts are check them at 3 to 3 1/2 hours to see if they need to be turned or moved. And chicken, with that particular sauce... really good with pasta. My family are fans of this and they don't care for mushroom soup. For the soup I used 1 10 1/2 oz can Cream of Mushroom with Garlic and 1 10 1/2 oz can Cream of Cremini & Shitake Mushroom soup. (Campbells). I added 3 cloves of fresh crushed garlic. Super good. Added the al dente ravioli the last 20 mins so as to not overcook. Thanks! Best base recipe and I give you credit!

For sure, please don't omit the "Golden Mushroom Soup" for "Cream of Mushroom", as there is a big difference in the taste. Also, don't leave out the white wine. It adds so much flavor. Always comes out great! You really can't switch out the white wine for chicken broth here, you are losing out on a better tasting dish if you do.

this was very good. I used 4oz block cream cheese and 4 oz onion/chive and more.mushrooms to use them up. Also added half n half in end to usenit up too. I added diced jalapeños and a little Sriracha in my bowl.for a kick. Added it to my favorites!!!

My husband loved it!! I ended up frying onions, garlic and mushrooms together in butter and then added it to about 15 oz. of water with a chicken bouillon cube instead of mushroom soup and added my own recipe of dry Italian style seasoning but otherwise, it was great!! Thanks!
Easy and delicious. My husband is a very picky eater. This recipe is one of his favorite meals.
The sauce came out too thin and it was too salty.

I agree with some users that this recipe can be salty so I make these changes to the ingredients. I use fresh mushrooms, cook them in the butter with some garlic, and use cream of celery soup, but I use the Healthy Request version which is half the sodium of the regular. Before adding the sauce to the crockpot, I like to add a good season each breast liberally with Bells Seasoning. No salt and it adds some Sage, Thyme, Rosemary and Black Pepper to the flavors. I also use the Good Seasons Zesty Italian dressing mix as it has about half the sodium as the regular Italian. The final addition is I like to cut up and add a rope of smoked sausage about an hour before I finish the cooking the chicken. Adds some more flavor (and probably more sodium but you can't have everything) and makes it more than a one note dish.

I used cream of mushroom soup as suggested by other reviewers. I found it somewhat bland. Very similar to a Chicken Stroganoff recipe from this site. I prefer that one over this one. Plus serving it over noodles would have been a better alternative than serving it over rice.
I used cream of chicken and cream cheese, I did pounded the chicken with seasoning first, and an hour before it was ready I shredded the chicken in the gravy
Simple, but extremely good
Easy to make and husband liked it.

I have made this dish about a dozen times now. It is delicious... but here's my twist! Instead of golden mushroom soup, I use mushroom soup with garlic. I also use plain cream cheese. This is because these are the ingredients that I had. It is sooo good! Last week I followed the recipe as written and I could not eat it! The golden mushroom soup kind of coagulated and would not mix well... something wasn't right. Please, if this recipe is not working for you try with regular mushroom soup with garlic. Also I add some mushrooms and grated cheese. It's also way too much liquid, I omit the wine and just add like a 1/4 cup chicken broth and not an entire 8 oz of cream cheese... I use maybe 6 oz. As written it just did not work for me, but I am so grateful for thr idea. We love it!
Everyone loved it. What great flavors and so easy... I made an adjustment and used Cream of Mushroom soup instead of Golden Mushroom. Will definitely keep this one in the rotation.
